PREMIUM AI+

It does not look at your chart. It reads it.

Send a screenshot to a general chatbot and it guesses from pixels. Ask AI is handed the measurements: where the liquidation pools sit, how much volume traded at which price, whether this volatility is high or low for this market, what the higher timeframe is doing, and where the unfilled gaps are. Then it draws the setup on your chart with the same tools a desk uses.

It also carries the one directional edge we have actually measured in our own data - and no screenshot can see it. Across 84 days of our own liquidations, after a capitulation that force-sold longs (strongest when open interest is unwinding at the same time) price leaned higher over the next one to four hours - about 60% of the time against a 50% coin flip, and higher in a true capitulation. When that fires the assistant leads with it; when there is no measured edge it tells you so plainly and reads the chart honestly instead of inventing a direction. We do not claim it wins every call - we claim it knows the difference.

WHY THE TWO PRICES ARE SO FAR APART

Premium costs us nothing to serve. Ask AI costs money every time it runs.

Everything else on this site - the indicators, the heatmap, the alerts, the boards - is code we already wrote. It serves a hundred members as cheaply as one. Ask AI is different: each read sends a measured brief to a frontier model and pays for it.

What one read costs us
$0.018

Measured on our own bills, per question on average; a full-length read at the model ceiling costs $0.044. At the Premium AI+ ceiling of 50 reads a day that is $27 to $66 a month of model spend for one member - which is why it is the only thing here with a per-use price, and why Premium carries five reads a day rather than fifty.

What the data alone costs elsewhere
$299 /month

Coinglass Standard, from their own pricing page. Hobbyist $29, Startup $79, Standard $299, Professional $699 - and no tier on that page includes AI analysis. That is the data delivered to you; reading it is still your job.

What a general AI subscription sees
A screenshot

A chatbot has no liquidation pools, no volume-at-price, no funding, no open interest and no idea whether this volatility is high or low for this market. It guesses from pixels, and it cannot draw a line on your chart. Ours is handed the measurements and draws the setup.

How to use it, in three steps

  1. Open Charts. Pick any coin and any timeframe - the AI reads the exact chart you are looking at, so what you choose is what it answers about.
  2. Press the AI button at the top of the chart. It sits in the toolbar beside the timeframe and the indicators, and it opens a chat panel on the right (a sheet from the bottom on a phone).
  3. Ask in your own words. "Find me an opportunity here", "where is my stop?", "draw the setup", "what is RSI?" - in any of the 13 site languages. It answers, and when you ask it to draw, it draws on the chart itself.

It can also work the chart for you: switch the timeframe, open an indicator, jump to another coin. Your conversation is kept per coin, so closing the panel or coming back tomorrow picks up where you left off. Each answer ends with an entry, a stop, targets and the reward-to-risk - and it says so plainly when the honest answer is to wait.

The 5 AI indicators

Four readouts built on data only MarginPad has - our own liquidation feed, the leverage ladder behind the heatmap, funding and crowd positioning - each answering one question you should ask before opening a position. Every arrow indicator also grades itself on the loaded chart (1.5x ATR target vs stop) and prints its own hit-rate, so you can see when it works here and when it does not.

Cascade Radar FRAGILITY

How easy is it for the market to fall (or rise) in a chain right now?

You see: one line from 0 to 100 under the candles, with a marker at 90, and a legend line that says which side the fuel sits on.

It means: under 50 the market is calm and this indicator has nothing to say. Rising past 70 it is fragile: enough leveraged positions sit close to price that one push can force-close them and the next ones in a chain. The legend tells you where the chain would run: fuel BELOW = it is longs that would be liquidated (price can fall fast), fuel ABOVE = shorts (price can squeeze up fast).

Before a long: line above 70 and fuel below = you would be buying on top of a trapdoor; wait for the flush, or take half size with a wider stop. Fuel above = the squeeze would run in your favour.
Before a short: the mirror - fuel below is your target zone, fuel above means you are the one standing on the trapdoor.
The arrow: red CASC over a candle = chain primed downwards; green CASC under a candle = primed upwards.

Big Liquidations (24h) REAL EVENTS, NOT A MODEL

Where has leverage actually been force-closed in the last 24 hours - and what happens when price goes back there?

You see: circles on the candles, at the exact price and the exact candle where a big liquidation happened in the last 24 hours. Red = a long was force-SOLD there. Green = a short was force-BOUGHT there. The bigger the circle, the bigger the position. Tap one for its size, the side in words, the venue it happened on and how far that price is from the price now.

It means: every other liquidation indicator you can buy anywhere is a guess, because the scripting languages on other charting sites cannot reach a liquidation feed at all. These are not guesses and not forecasts - they are events our own collector recorded across nine exchanges. Where they cluster is where leverage actually died: that is where the stops sat, and where the market proved somebody was offside. A band of red circles under a drop is the cascade that caused it. It covers the ten coins our feed records - BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE, BNB, ADA, LINK, AVAX and LTC; on any other market it cannot be switched on and says it has no data.

Before a long: price coming back DOWN into a thick band of red circles is arriving where forced selling already happened once - either it gets absorbed and that is your level, or it breaks and the same thing happens again. Green circles above you mark where shorts were squeezed out, so a move back up through them has fuel behind it.
Before a short: the mirror. Shorting into a band of green circles is shorting where shorts were already force-closed once. An empty chart means the market has been calm - which is information too.

Liquidation Magnet TARGETS

Where is price likely to go and touch next?

You see: two horizontal lines on the price - a red one above (where shorts get liquidated) and a green one below (where longs get liquidated). The bold one is the stronger magnet; each carries its size in dollars.

It means: price is drawn to the bigger pool of forced orders first, because forced orders move a market that nobody else is moving. The bold line is the likelier next visit, and the legend prints how far away both are.

Before a long: bold line above you = your first target, take some profit there. Bold line below you = expect a dip to it first; put your stop under that line, not just above it, or you are the order that gets hunted.
Before a short: the mirror - bold green line below is the target, bold red line above means keep the stop beyond it.
No lines: both sides were already flushed; nothing is pulling, expect a slower market.

Market Brain ADAPTIVE

Which way does the evidence lean, and how much should you trust it here?

You see: a line from -100 to +100 with two bands at +55 and -55, a legend line "driven by: X + Y", and a chip like BRAIN 58% (14W/10L).

It means: the line going up = the evidence is leaning bullish, going down = bearish. It blends eight things (trend, momentum, volume, fragility, real liquidations, funding, crowd positioning, structure) and, every few candles, re-checks which of them actually predicted this coin on this timeframe, so a factor that does not work here counts for nothing. Inside the bands the model has no strong opinion. "Driven by" names the two reasons behind the number.

Before a long: you want the line above +55, or rising through it. Below -55 you are trading against the learned evidence - do not.
Before a short: the mirror, below -55.
Inside the bands: no edge here - size down or use the Magnet levels instead.
The chip: the percentage is how often its arrows worked on this exact chart. Under 50% = the model has no edge on this coin and timeframe; ignore its arrows there, whatever the line does.

Market Memory FORECAST

The last 25 times it looked like this, what happened next?

You see: a purple line under the candles (the expected move), a dashed MEM line on the price at the projected level, and a legend like 25 analogs · 72% up · proj +1.4% / 6 bars.

It means: it found the 25 past moments that most resembled right now and reports what price did in the six candles after them. 72% up and +1.4% = most of those moments went up, by about that much. It is a base rate, not a call.

Before a long: 65% up or more AND a projected move bigger than your fees and stop = go, with the MEM line as a realistic target and six candles as the horizon (six hours on a 1h chart).
Before a short: the mirror, 35% up or less.
45-55%: history went both ways from here - a coin flip. Stay out, or trade the Magnet levels instead of a direction.
The arrow: MEMO fires only when the analogs agree; it is the strongest form of this readout.
